purpose: Assess ASVS V12 Secure Communication, and record the governance finding that the production TLS configuration is not under version control.
requiredInvariants: No PASS is inferred from what Caddy does by default, or from a configuration file that is not the production terminator.
infra/nginx/nginx.conf must never be cited as evidence about production.
A requirement whose verification needs the live endpoint is recorded APPLICABLE and NOT_ASSESSED with the blocker named - never PASS, never FAIL.
The internal-transport FAIL must name the Istio STRICT mTLS policy and explain why it does not apply, or the finding would mislead.
FAIL is recorded and reported, never resolved by editing product logic or infrastructure.
No product logic, dependency, production, REG.RU, DNS or database change.
acceptance: The absence of the production TLS configuration from version control is recorded as an explicit finding in the threat model.
V12.1.1, V12.1.2, V12.1.4, V12.1.5, V12.2.1 and V12.2.2 are NOT_ASSESSED with the blocker named, not PASS and not FAIL.
V12.3.2 PASS rests on both an explicit rejectUnauthorized: true and a tree-wide proof that verification is never disabled.
V12.3.1 and V12.3.3 name Istio and explain why a mesh policy does not wrap Docker Compose on a single virtual server.
V12.1.3 is justified non-applicable on a machine-checked absence of client-certificate identity handling, and prose mentions of mTLS are not mistaken for code.
A requirement blocked on unreachable evidence is provably neither PASS nor FAIL, and still blocks finalPass.
The concurrent-scope guard accepts exactly the four authorized paths.
